summary: Private VPC: idp-assertion CRLF in 'roles' attribute truncates RBAC list, causing 403s for admins and batch workers
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports admin users and scheduled batch workers receiving 403 Forbidden when attempting to access the Redwood Console and when scheduled inference jobs start. Symptoms began after an IdP change that added logging metadata into an attribute.

Impact:
- Multiple customer admins cannot access console for tenant cedar-financial (several 403s).
- Scheduled batch workers fail during token-exchange phase and are retrying; data-processing jobs stalled.
- Severity: operationally blocking for customer-run workloads (P1 / Sev1).

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) managed by Redwood private control plane.
- Region: us-west.
- Affected services: private-idp-proxy, auth-proxy, rbac-service.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer authenticates through their on-prem IdP (SAML) with roles attribute containing an appended log-note that includes a CRLF sequence ("roleA\r\nnote:errored-at=...\r\nroleB").
2) Redwood private-idp-proxy receives assertion and forwards attributes to auth-proxy.
3) Token exchange succeeds but RBAC service reads the 'roles' attribute and stops parsing at the first CR/LF, only mapping roleA into bindings.
4) Users and service accounts expecting multiple roles lose required admin or worker bindings and receive 403s.

Observed logs (redacted):
- private-idp-proxy: "Received SAML assertion for user=alice@cedar.example.com roles=\"roleA\r\nnote:job=123\r\nroleB\""
- auth-proxy: "Forwarding attributes to rbac-service: roles=\"roleA\""
- rbac-service: "No admin binding found for principal alice@cedar.example.com -> deny 403"

Expected behavior:
- Roles attribute should be parsed as a single logical attribute containing multiple comma/semicolon separated role identifiers or as a structured list. CRLFs inside attribute values should be sanitized or preserved as literal characters without truncating the role list.

Temporary workaround (applied):
- Customer rolled back the IdP change to stop injecting multi-line notes into roles attribute.
- Support added a temporary request header mapping in the private-idp-proxy to replace CRLF sequences in the roles attribute with a single space for affected tenant. This unblocks access while a permanent fix is planned.

Next steps requested:
- SRE to implement resilient parsing in rbac-service (normalize and split roles on known delimiters then ignore CR/LF sequences embedded inside values).
- Product to document acceptable attribute formats in private onboarding runbook.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Customer opened after onboarding change introduced two admin users getting 403s and batch workers failing. Customer shared SAML assertion sample (redacted) showing CRLF sequences inside roles attribute.

2026-03-13 10:01 - SRE (Marcus): Confirmed reproduction in staging using redacted assertion. RBAC parser currently uses line-based splitting that treats CR/LF as separator; this truncates downstream attribute payload. Assigning to eng for parser hardening.
2026-03-13 14:30 - Customer (SRE contact): Customer applied rollback of IdP config as temporary mitigation and reports console access restored for admins. Batch jobs resumed as well.

2026-03-14 08:45 - Eng (Nina Rodriguez): Adding note — edge-proxy already has a small normalization filter but it runs after we canonicalize attributes; ordering needs adjustment. Proposing to move normalization earlier and add tolerant parsing in rbac-service.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: ingress/edge-proxy header normalization strips subsequent lines after CR/LF leading to truncated attribute before RBAC evaluation.

Hypothesis 2: rbac-service uses naive split on '\n' without normalizing '\r\n' and stops at first item; will verify code paths.
Action: instrument rbac-service to log raw attribute bytes for tenant cedar-financial in staging.

Findings: staging reproduction shows edge-proxy forwards 'roles' trimmed at first CR/LF. private-idp-proxy logged raw assertion containing CRLF sequences. Edge-proxy normalization filter was configured to 'protect against header injections' and removed everything after first CRLF. That behavior is overly aggressive for multi-valued assertion attributes.
Risk: Patch must be careful to avoid reintroducing header-injection vectors. We need a targeted normalization only for attribute payloads coming from IdP assertions, not generic header passthroughs.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: tenant-scoped normalization rule in private-idp-proxy replaced CRLF sequences in roles attribute with space; customer rolled back IdP change and regained access (verified 2026-03-13 14:50).

Short-term fix: Adjust edge-proxy to stop truncating attributes on CRLF for SAML assertion-derived headers; add sanitizer that maps CRLF->U+2028 (line separator) when attribute seen and logged for parity. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/3124.

Long-term fix: rbac-service to accept and normalize attributes by splitting on allowed delimiters (comma, semicolon, space) and ignoring embedded control characters. Engineering to include unit tests and a migration plan. Target ETA: 2026-03-21.

Follow-ups: Update private onboarding docs to include 'roles' attribute canonicalization rules and add a check in the onboarding validation script to detect multi-line values. Assign owner: Nina Rodriguez (Platform) for rollout.
